A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Visionary-R1 research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across formatting changes and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original Visionary-R1 training and evaluation, implemented SFT/GRPO comparisons, component ablations, and KL-schedule experiments in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds a caption-length control, additional benchmark evaluations, model-scaling results, and reward-weight analysis.

M1.justification: The caption-reason-answer procedure, caption reward, GRPO objective, and cosine-annealed KL penalty remain unchanged. Both appendix prompts are retained. The new length reward appears only as an experimental control, and the 7B experiment applies the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 substantially broadens evaluation with MMMUPro and CV-Bench's 2D and 3D tests in Table 5. The four original benchmarks remain represented, including MMStar in the appendix. The 11-dataset, 272.6K-pair training mixture is unchanged.

E2.justification: The MMStar comparison is substantially reconfigured: most commercial and open-model comparisons from v1 Table 1 disappear, while v2 Table 5 retains R1-VL and adds R1-Onevision results and separate 7B base-model comparisons. Table 2 adds a length-reward control. Comparator membership for the three retained Table 1 benchmarks is unchanged.

E3.justification: Added configurations include a controlled 3B/7B comparison using 17.1K A-OKVQA training examples, caption-reward weights of 0.1 versus 0.5, and a length-reward control. These supplement the existing evaluation design; the original main-training hyperparameters and named test splits are not revised.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses testing whether caption length alone explains improvements, whether the method transfers to a 7B model, and sensitivity to caption-reward weight (Tables 2, 6, and 7). Table 3 extends KL-schedule analysis to MMStar and MMBench. The existing qualitative examples in Figures 8–14 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. v2's statement of 'no significant difference' between reward weights does not specify any statistical testing procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and new Tables 5–7 add substantial benchmark and analysis results. For example, the 7B A-OKVQA-trained model scores 70.2/24.4/66.7/89.5 on MathVista/MathVision/MMStar/MMBench. The reported main 3B MMStar score changes from 66.5 in v1 Table 1 to 61.5 in v2 Table 5, without explaining whether conditions changed. Figure 2 also revises reasoning-length coordinates. Retained Table 1 scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same reward definition, group-relative advantage, optimization objective, KL penalty, and cosine schedule. No new formal assumptions, theorems, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims about GRPO shortcut learning, caption-first reasoning without CoT supervision, and strong visual-reasoning performance. Additional benchmarks and scaling evidence support the existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: v2 attributes the length-reward control's poorer performance to redundancy, interprets additional benchmark improvements as broader generalization, and recommends reward weight 0.1 for stability. It removes the explicit 3B-only limitation while adding 7B experiments. The earlier explanations of shortcut learning and KL-related failures remain.

D1.justification: v2 removes v1's disclosure of approximately 1,500 GPU hours on NVIDIA A800-80G GPUs. Core hyperparameters, training-data composition, both full prompts, the repository URL, and the promise of future code/model release remain available.

R1.justification: Related work adds Pixel Reasoner and VL-Rethinker, contrasting their reliance on SFT and data preparation with Visionary-R1's pure-RL approach. References for MMMU-Pro and Cambrian-1/CV-Bench are also added. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized discussion additions, author-year citations, the displayed author name changing from Yixuan Li to Sharon Li, and appendix reorganization: new experimental and LLM-use sections precede the retained visualization section.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially expanded and reorganized: Table 1 loses its MMStar column, Table 2 gains a control row, Table 3 gains two benchmark columns, and Tables 5–7 are added. Figure 2 is redrawn with a wider reasoning-length axis. The document template and appendix figure placement also change.

improvement.justification: The length-reward control tests a relevant alternative explanation, and the 7B experiment partly addresses v1's explicit model-scale limitation. These provide useful validation beyond merely adding benchmark scores. The gains are limited by removed hardware/compute information, narrower MMStar comparisons, and unexplained revisions to the MMStar score and Figure 2 reasoning lengths.
